newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Ghost economy cuts Bangladesh revenue.
newsitem.headline: Ghost economy cuts Bangladesh revenue.

text.p: Bangladesh has an underground economy that is twice as big as the country's gross domestic product (GDP) and evades taxes worth $6 billion annually, economists said.

Kabir Hassan, associate professor at the New Orleans University in the United States, said on Sunday the underground economy (UE) deprived the Bangladesh government of tax revenues that amounted to roughly 23 percent of the country's GDP.
Hassan, a Bangladeshi, released a report at a seminar in Dhaka showing the underground economy in the export and import sectors averaged 1.7 percent and 9.1 percent respectively of the country's GDP.
Government officials said traders evaded export and import duties by distorting the value of the goods.
"These results suggest that the UE is big enough for the policymakers to take a serious look at it," he said.
He said Bangladesh could reduce the growth of the underground economy by liberalising foreign trade, especially imports.
Hassan said: "Encouraging private investment by opening more investment opportunities in the formal sector would also help stop the leakage into the UE."
He called for fiscal discipline and tax reform to restrain the growth of the underground economy.
"A long-run strategy based on sustained efforts and economic liberalisation and fiscal discipline will be effective in achieving this objective (plugging the leakage)," he said.
